newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-FIRST PERU CLUB IN LIBERTADORES SEMIS FOR DECADES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIRST PERU CLUB IN LIBERTADORES SEMIS FOR DECADES.

text.p: Sporting Cristal on Wednesday became the first Peruvian club in over 20 years to qualify for the semi-finals of the South American Libertadores Cup when they beat Bolivia's Bolivar 4-2 over two legs.

The Peruvian champions, who inflicted a shock quarter-final defeat on Argentina's Velez Sarsfield reversed a 2-1 first leg defeat with a comfortable 3-0 home win on Wednesday in a tie between two of the tournament's least fancied sides.

"This is incredible. Cristal is one of the top four clubs in South America," Sergio Makarian shouted to reporters at the final whistle as a capacity crowd of 41,000 fans exploded in celebration in the National Stadium.

Cristal will now represent Peru, which has never won the tournament, against one of the powerhouses of South American football, Argentina's Racing Club, who sneaked past Uruguay's Penarol on 3-2 penalties in their quarter-final tie.

The eventual winner of the continent's premier club tournament will earn the right to play the newly-crowned European Cup winners, Germany's Borussia Dortmund, in the Intercontinental Cup to decide the world's best team.
